[0] everyday_reading (E): In everyday text a backslash is just a character, and a new line is made by pressing Enter. Inside a Java literal a backslash starts an escape: \n is one newline character and \\ is one backslash, and a literal cannot contain a raw line break.
[1] misconception (M) -> EscapeIsTwoCharacters: wrong rule: \t in a string prints a backslash and the letter t. Right rule: A backslash starts an escape sequence, so \t is a single tab character.
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> EscapeIsTwoCharacters: Points to LT (the compiler turns each escape into a single character). Applied unevenly, a student prints "\n" as a line break but counts it as two characters in length() or charAt. (here mixing in: "\t in a string prints a backslash and the letter t")

[0] names_the_element (N): Escape sequence: a backslash code inside a char or String literal that stands for one special character (\t, \n, \\, \', \").
[1] states_the_rule (S): Java has eight escape sequences. The common ones are \t (tab), \n (newline), \\ (backslash), \' (single quote) and \" (double quote), and each represents a single character.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): The compiler replaces each escape with its single character while reading the literal, so at run time the String already contains that one character.
[1] output_prediction (OP): System.out.print("Hello!
How are you doing?
") prints two lines. "a	b" prints a, a tab, then b. "Hi
".length() is 3.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): An escape changes no variable. Printing 
 moves the output position to the start of a new line.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): Escapes are written inside "..." or '...'. \" puts a double quote inside a String literal without ending it.
[1] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Escapes format output (line breaks, tab-aligned columns) and put quote or backslash characters into text.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> EscapeIsTwoCharacters: Removing the backslash turns \n into the letter n. Doubling it (\\n) prints a backslash followed by n. Adding a space after \n puts a space at the start of the next line.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Use escapes for special characters inside literals. For line ends in formatted output, use println or printf's %n, which gives the platform line separator.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: A double quote inside a String literal must be escaped. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: An unescaped " inside a String, such as "She said "Hi"": the literal ends early, and the compiler reports an unclosed literal or ')' expected.
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: A backslash must be followed by a valid escape character. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: Backslash plus an undefined letter, e.g. a Windows path "C:\data": 'illegal escape character'.
[4] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: A backslash followed by a valid escape letter is replaced by that character. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: Paths or text containing \t or \n by accident ("C:\temp" contains a tab).
